lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Which One Is Better? Comparing Cities and Hotels
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leão | Lesson 23 -- Which One Is Better?
lesson.grammar_point: comparative adjectives (-er than, more than, better, worse)

listenings.text: I lived in Lisbon for two years, and now I live in Berlin. People always ask me: which city is better? Well, Lisbon is warmer and sunnier, of course. Berlin is colder, but it is bigger and more modern. Lisbon is cheaper, and the food is better. Sorry, Berlin! But Berlin is quieter at night, and the trains are faster. And the people? In Lisbon they are friendlier on the street. In Berlin they are more direct. My answer? Lisbon is more beautiful, but Berlin is easier for my work. So I'll stay here, for now.

This week I stayed in two hotels in Copenhagen. The first one, the Harbor Hotel, was bigger and more modern. The rooms were cleaner, and the view of the water was better. But it was more expensive, and it was farther from the center, twenty minutes by bus. The second one, the Garden Hotel, was smaller and older. But it was cozier, and the people at the desk were friendlier. It was also cheaper, and closer to the restaurants. My choice for next time? The Garden Hotel. Smaller, but happier.

extra_audio.text: Copenhagen is warmer than Oslo in May. The Garden Hotel is cheaper than the Harbor Hotel. The Harbor Hotel is more modern, but it is farther from the center. The Garden Hotel is cozier and friendlier. So we'll stay at the Garden Hotel.
